drug_class: BTK inhibitor (Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor) — a type of targeted cancer therapy
purpose: Pirtobrutinib is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including mantle cell lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). It is typically used when other treatments have already been tried. Your doctor prescribed it because it targets the specific type of cancer cells in your body.
how_it_works: Think of cancer cells as having an 'on switch' called BTK that tells them to keep growing and multiplying. Pirtobrutinib works by blocking that switch, so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow. This helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading. It is a very targeted approach, meaning it goes after the cancer cells more specifically than traditional chemotherapy.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include tiredness or fatigue, bruising more easily than usual, muscle or joint pain, diarrhea, and a higher chance of getting infections. You may also notice some swelling or shortness of breath. Most side effects are manageable, but always let your doctor or pharmacist know if anything bothers you.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious bleeding, so tell your doctor if you take blood thinners or notice unusual bleeding. It can also raise your risk of serious infections, including pneumonia. Pirtobrutinib may cause heart rhythm problems (irregular heartbeat), so report any chest fluttering or pounding. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication. Do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, since many drugs can interact with pirtobrutinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 200 mg (two 100 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day — but if it is already the next day, just skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Never take two doses in one day.
